title: Setting Up Python Environment
description: Learn how to install Python, set up an IDE, run scripts, and configure your development environment for a smooth coding experience.

lessons.title: Downloading and Installing Python
lessons.content: Visit https://www.python.org/downloads to download Python. Choose your OS (Windows, macOS, Linux) and install it. During installation on Windows, check the option 'Add Python to PATH'.

lessons.title: Verifying Python Installation
lessons.content:
Open terminal or command prompt and type:
```
python --version
```
You should see the installed Python version (e.g., Python 3.11.0).

lessons.title: Setting Up VS Code for Python
lessons.content: Download VS Code from https://code.visualstudio.com/. Install the Python extension from the Extensions Marketplace. Configure the interpreter using `Ctrl+Shift+P` > 'Python: Select Interpreter'.

lessons.title: Alternative Editors: PyCharm, Thonny, Jupyter
lessons.content:
- **PyCharm**: Powerful IDE by JetBrains, best for large projects.
- **Thonny**: Beginner-friendly IDE.
- **Jupyter Notebook**: Ideal for data science and quick visual code.

lessons.title: Running Python in Terminal
lessons.content:
To enter interactive mode, type `python` in terminal:
```
>>> print("Hello, Python!")
Hello, Python!
```

lessons.title: Writing and Running Python Scripts
lessons.content:
Create a file named `hello.py`:
```python
print("Hello, World!")
```
Then run it using:
```
python hello.py
```

lessons.title: Understanding Python File Structure
lessons.content: Python scripts end with `.py`. You can organize code into modules (files) and packages (folders with `__init__.py` files) for better structure in bigger projects.

lessons.title: Using pip to Manage Packages
lessons.content:
`pip` is Python’s package installer. Example:
```
pip install requests
```
Use `pip list` to view installed packages.

lessons.title: Installing Python on macOS and Linux
lessons.content:
- **macOS**: Use Homebrew: `brew install python`
- **Linux**: Use package manager like `apt` or `yum`: `sudo apt install python3`
Always verify installation with `python3 --version`.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting Setup Issues
lessons.content:
- Check PATH variable
- Use `python3` if `python` points to Python 2
- Reinstall or use the official installer if issues persist
- Use forums like Stack Overflow or the Python Discord for help
